subject: Next steps: PoC contingency plan & deployment mode decision
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medlytics.ai>, Alex Byrne <alexb@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: PoC contingency plan & deployment mode decision — quick recap

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to understand Medlytics' throughput profile and the PHI constraints you mentioned. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight PoC contingency plan so we can lock the deployment mode decision. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Call recap (high-level)
- Primary workload: real-time chart summarization from streaming clinical notes (~800 reqs/min peak, 2–4 concurrent processes).
- Data sensitivity: PHI in requests; customer must maintain control over keys and audit logs.
- Performance target: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- SLA expectation: 99.9% availability during business hours.

Deployment mode constraints (we heard)
- Preferred: Private VPC/on-prem if we can meet your switchover and onboarding window (security and KMS integration are musts).
- Acceptable alternative: Dedicated capacity with strict network isolation (private peering) plus signed SOC2 + contractual audit rights.
- Hosted API: only acceptable for non-PHI synthetic testing or sandboxing.

Proposed PoC contingency plan (goal: determine final deployment mode within 3 weeks)
1) Week 0 (this week) — alignment call: confirm stakeholders, RSA access for security docs. Owners: Karthik (Redwood), Sarah (Medlytics).
2) Week 1 — Security & compliance fast-pass: exchange Medlytics security questionnaire; Redwood sends Private VPC and Dedicated compliance checklist. Owners: Marissa (Redwood Security liaison), Legal Ops (Medlytics).
3) Week 2 — Technical dry-run: short synthetic workload run in Hosted sandbox to validate latency assumptions and token accounting. Non-PHI data only. Owners: Stephanie (Redwood Solutions), Alex (Medlytics Eng).
4) Week 3 — Pilot readiness: either (a) provision Private VPC trial image + KMS test, or (b) allocate Dedicated pool with private peering. Decision gate: security sign-off.

Proposed success criteria (PoC sign-off)
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms on representative synthetic set.
- Cost signal: per-token cost estimate within 15% of forecast.
- Security: KMS integration validated; audit logs flowing to Medlytics' SIEM; contract addendum agreed.
- Ops: can autoscale to 1.5x peak without increased latency.

Immediate asks
- Sarah: confirm stakeholders (security, infra, legal) and available times for an alignment call this Friday.
- Alex: a short sample of the token distribution (histogram) you mentioned — ok to share sanitized CSV?

Attachments: I attached the PoC checklist and the security questionnaire we discussed.

If Private VPC is a hard requirement, we’ll fast-track security and bump the timeline for environment provisioning by 2–3 days. Otherwise we’ll default to starting with the sandbox validation.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendars once I hear back.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), medlytics_security_questions.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medlytics.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Byrne <alexb@medlytics.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@medlytics.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PoC contingency plan & deployment mode decision — quick recap

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Stakeholders confirmed: me (Product/AI), Alex (Infra/Eng), Priya R. (Security), and Legal Ops (cc'd). Priya prefers Private VPC but will evaluate Dedicated if we get demonstrable KMS control and contract terms for audit access.
- Token distribution: Alex will share a sanitized histogram (non-PHI) by end of day.
- Timeline constraints: we need the decision completed before Mar 20 due to vendor onboarding windows with our procurement. 3-week path works if we start this week.

Next steps from us:
- Priya will send a short list of non-negotiable security items (KMS, customer-managed keys, log retention).
- Legal Ops will review any addendum; please share a sample SOC2 + Dedicated isolation SLA doc.

Questions: if we request Private VPC, what is the earliest you can provide a test image and network diagram? Also, are there extra licensing or infra fees we should anticipate in the PoC phase?

Thanks,
Sarah
Director of Product, Medlytics
sarah.lin@medlytics.ai

On Thu, 25 Feb 2027 at 09:22, Alex Byrne <alexb@medlytics.ai> wrote:
> Karthik / Sarah — I attached the sanitized histogram (token_distribution_q1.csv).
> —Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Alex Byrne <alexb@medlytics.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PoC contingency plan & deployment mode decision — alignment and next steps

Thanks for the updates, all. Quick answers from our side to help Priya / Legal: 

- Private VPC test image: we can deliver a VPC trial image (OVF) and a network diagram in 5 business days from sign-off. That includes basic KMS test harness for customer-managed keys.
- Dedicated pool notes: Dedicated capacity requires a 30-day lead to provision at our core sites; for the PoC we can offer a temporary Dedicated slice (short-term) with private peering, but there is a small provisioning fee (I'll include numbers in the attached cost rubric).
- SOC2 / isolation docs: attaching a short SOC2 summary and a Dedicated isolation SLA excerpt for Legal to review.

If Medlytics prefers the fastest route to validating latency/cost, recommend starting Week 1 with Hosted sandbox (non-PHI) while we queue Private VPC provisioning in parallel. That gives you empirical numbers to compare without PHI exposure.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Monday: 30-minute alignment call to confirm sign-off and exchange access tokens.
- Tuesday-Wednesday: Hosted sandbox run (non-PHI) — Redwood provides test harness.
- By end of next week: Private VPC test image delivered if sign-off confirmed.

I’ll paste the cost rubrics and SOC2 summary in a separate email to Legal.

—
Marissa Cole
Security & Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: redwood_dedicated_sla_excerpt.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, redwood_cost_rubric.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Alex Byrne <alexb@medlytics.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@medlytics.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PoC contingency plan & deployment mode decision — alignment and next steps

Great — thanks everyone. Short note to lock in the alignment call:

Proposed meeting: Tue Mar 1, 10:00–10:30 PT (30m) — quick alignment and go/no-go for Private VPC provisioning.
Agenda:
- Confirm stakeholders and decision gate (5m)
- Review sanitized token histogram and latency target (10m)
- Confirm security must-haves and sign-off approach (10m)
- Logistics: who executes provisioning request and timeline (5m)

If that slot works for Medlytics, I’ll send a calendar invite and drop a short meeting doc (intent: record owners and decision criteria).

Note on cost: Marissa will follow with the cost rubric, but expect a small one-time infra provisioning fee for Private VPC test images. No hidden licensing; Dedicated pool carries a short-term charge if used in PoC. We’ll include a written cost estimate before any provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the mode decision quickly so we can scope the full pilot.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
